title: Treatment Benefits (Special Access) (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2019
short_title: Treatment Benefits (Special Access) (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would adapt tax, health and compensation laws to support special treatment access for eligible members of Australian civilian surgical and medical teams in Vietnam.
Eligible recipients would gain Medicare levy relief under existing exemption rules, while travel reimbursements and pharmaceutical supplements under the companion scheme would be income-tax exempt.
Its transitional rules would apply treatment, travel expenses and pharmaceutical supplements from 1 July 2019, with both schedules dependent on commencement of the companion legislation.
changes: Protected aged-care information could be disclosed to Veterans' Affairs for administering the new treatment arrangements.
Overlapping pharmaceutical supplements under specified military compensation and social security payments would be prevented.
Comcare medical expense compensation would generally stop for recipients whose treatment eligibility is established, subject to an exceptional-circumstances determination.
Existing medical compensation eligibility would be preserved until 1 July 2019 where the new treatment claim was determined earlier.
summary.affected: Eligible Australian civilian surgical and medical team members, Veterans' Affairs and Comcare are affected.

speeches.speaker: Karen Andrews
speeches.brief: The Treatment Benefits (Special Access) (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2019 amends related acts to allow civilian surgical and medical team members to receive medical treatment and pharmaceutical supplements under the Treatment Benefits (Special Access) Act 2019, and ensures they transition smoothly from the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988 while exempting them from income tax on travel expenses and pharmaceutical benefits.

speeches.speaker: Amanda Rishworth
speeches.brief: The speaker argued for the Treatment Benefits (Special Access) Bill 2019, which extends gold card health coverage to approximately 240 doctors, 210 nurses, and other civilian medical staff who served in Vietnam from 1964 to 1972, and urged the government to reject the Productivity Commission's recommendation to dismantle the Department of Veterans' Affairs.

speeches.speaker: Nicolle Flint
speeches.brief: The Treatment Benefits (Special Access) Bill 2019 and related bill extend Department of Veterans' Affairs gold card health benefits to surviving civilian surgical and medical team members who served in Vietnam alongside the ADF, benefiting about 200 people from 1 July 2019. The speaker highlighted the service of nurses like Helen Taplin and Betty Lockwood, and noted the legislation provides recognition and medical treatment for any condition, including mental health support.
